fixtureBoundary.runtime: Installed official 0.2.1-rc.3 public packages; native Node process
fixtureBoundary.agentContext: The fixture mints caller contexts through public createScope; mount and composeFrom bind them to the actual registry-owned standing generation.
fixtureBoundary.previousFixtureGap: The previous primitive fixture registered tools and restriction into the same scope that it observed. It omitted the standing preset generation and the actual Agent child scope.

source.inspection: Read-only git show of the exact tag; the source checkout HEAD differs from the tag.

references.finding: activate creates a registry-owned standing scope and mounts the configured plugin tree into it.
mount and composeFrom parent actual Agent scope keys to the standing generation key.
mountPreset uses the scoped context to construct and load the Loader tree.
Entry context refresh inherits its parent context; it does not mint an Agent scope.
Include adds a file-backed EntryTree and changes resolution base; its children retain the standing scope.
ScopedLayers reads the complete ancestry chain and places registrations into scopeOf(ctx).
view treats standing-preset tools as inherited for the actual Agent, applies every ancestor restriction, and exempts only the exact viewing scope own registrations.
ReactLoopAgent mints its own scope with createScope before preset binding.
The Agent factory executes setup with the newly created Agent context before publication.

publicInterfaceAudit.result: Only identity, display metadata and plugins are declared; no Host-global tool-origin selector exists.
These public paths bind or inherit a standing generation. They do not accept a tool-origin restriction option.
Config controls presentation and parallel subcalls; ToolRestriction contains only tool-name allow and deny lists.
isolate selects service realms; it does not select global versus standing-preset tool registrations.
The tool rejects toolFilter configuration and directs capability composition to Presets.

causalConclusion: The standing generation owns both the Preset tools and allow:[] restriction. Actual Agents inherit that generation. Tools.view applies the standing restriction to those inherited Preset tools, producing the observed empty model tool list.
integrationConclusion: The inspected official public interfaces cannot express the required dynamic Host-global-only mask at the standing Preset boundary while preserving that Preset tools for actual parent and child Agents.

choices.action: Complete the official host restriction contract for registration origin/layer, publish that host capability, then verify the existing single declaration through the retained failing regression and Desktop.
Obtain an explicit requirement change to permit inherited Host-global tools before removing the restriction. The control output confirms both Host-global and Preset tools become visible.
